sources.source: Gao–Zhao, Tight Entropy Contraction of Generalized Quantum Depolarization
sources.own_synthesis: E* acts on observables; E is its trace-dual channel, not generally unital. Definition3.7 optimizes D(Phi(rho)||E(rho))/D(rho||E(rho)) for positive retained weight. Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.3 concern that ratio and its large-index behavior, not the two-variable budgeted coefficient. Proposition3.11 gives one pure index witness commuting with its image; it does not assert two orthogonal witnesses with the same image. Selected hypotheses and proofs therefore do not literally cover1017. A global index and a restricted family order budget are distinct.

sources.source: Hirche–Rouzé–Stilck França, On contraction coefficients, partial orders and approximation of capacities for quantum channels
sources.own_synthesis: These selected passages give the physical depolarizing parameter range and a comparison of ordinary less-noisy channels. The proof reduces an ordinary depolarizing relative-entropy comparison to commuting eigenvalue data. It does not state the same-reference ancillary constrained profile1017; no claim about other unread sections.

sources.source: Cao–Lu, Tensorization of the strong data processing inequality for quantum chi-square divergences
sources.own_synthesis: Theorem1 assumes a product reference and either the geometric weight x^-1/2 or suitable weights with quantum-classical channels. Those hypotheses differ from arbitrary entangled same-reference inputs and SLD minimal weight. Reading the theorem and definitions is not a proof audit or evidence that every part of the paper lacks a related result.
